correctness.rationale: On P^1(F_q), the number of degree-2 and degree-3 closed points is (q²−q)/2 and (q³−q)/3; dividing their product by |PGL₂(F_q)|=q(q²−1) yields the weighted orbit mass q(q−1)/6. A stabilizer injects into the centralizer C3 of the Frobenius 3-cycle on the cubic roots, so has order 1 or 3. An order-3 element fixing the quadratic pair exists only in the nonsplit q≡2(mod3) case. There are q(q−1) nonsplit order-3 elements, each fixes one quadratic closed point and 2(q+1)/3 cubic closed points by the separable twisted-Frobenius equation; double-counting the two nontrivial stabilizers per exceptional divisor gives |PGL₂|/3 exceptional divisors, precisely one exceptional orbit. All remaining orbits are free, proving both formulas. The explicit z²−z+1 times cubic construction follows by the same Frob-twist. Independently enumerated actual PGL₂ orbit actions for q=5 over 400 quadratic/cubic pairs: exactly three free orbits and one order-3 orbit. The finite check corroborates rather than proves the prime-power theorem.
